_note: Signatures for ts-bench v1 exercises. Exercism stubs mostly say `unknown` or have no parameters, so a stub-derived F is useless as a contract. Each `type` below was written by hand from the call sites in the exercise's test file (argument and expectation shapes only, never a solution). OpenArc (A/B/C) and the baseline (D) get exactly the same typed signatures. `types` holds extra project-local types the signature needs.

flatten-array.types: export interface Nested extends Array<number | null | undefined | Nested> {}
flatten-array._note: interface form on purpose: the equivalent `type Nested = Array<number | null | undefined | Nested>` makes open-arc 0.6.3's Example<F> fail with TS2589 on the spec itself (pilot run used it; see results/2026-10-31-untuned-ollama-pilot/summary.md)

fns.degreesOfSeparation: (familyTree: FamilyTree, personA: string, personB: string) => number

skipped.anagram: class Anagram(input).matches(...words): constructor state + method; mappable only through a hand-written wrapper class, which the baseline would not get
skipped.bank-account: stateful class (open/close/deposit/withdraw/balance) with a custom error type; no function region fits
skipped.binary-search-tree: recursive mutable class with getters; no function region fits
skipped.bowling: stateful class (roll/score) whose behaviour depends on call history; examples are single calls with JSON args
skipped.complex-numbers: value class with getters and methods returning new instances; examples cannot construct class instances
skipped.connect: class Board(board).winner(); mappable only through a wrapper class
skipped.crypto-square: class Crypto(text).ciphertext getter; mappable only through a wrapper class
skipped.dnd-character: static methods, one uses randomness (effect 'random'); tests are statistical
skipped.pascals-triangle: class Triangle(n) with rows/lastRow getters; mappable only through a wrapper class
skipped.rational-numbers: value class; tests chain methods on instances
skipped.react: reactive closures (createInput/createComputed/createCallback) with shared module state; examples cannot express subscriptions
skipped.robot-name: stateful class with global name registry and randomness; tests use beforeEach/afterEach
skipped.two-bucket: class with constructor parameters and getters; mappable only through a wrapper class
